meta.title: Roster — Your coding agents, in a room
meta.description: A macOS app that shows your Claude Code sessions as colleagues in a blueprint office. They work at their desks — and walk to yours when they're done. Free, open source, local-only.

hero.title: Your coding agents, in a room.
hero.subtitle: Roster turns your Claude Code sessions into colleagues in a small blueprint office. They work at their stations. They stand up when they need you. And when they finish, they cross the room to your desk.
hero.note: macOS 14+ · Signed & notarized · No account, no telemetry
hero.caption: Live from the room — dockkeep just finished and is waiting at your desk.

positioning.title: Not another dashboard.
positioning.body: Lists, diffs, kanban boards — other tools already do that well. Roster is the ambient version: a quiet room in the corner of your screen. You don't read it, you glance at it. The state of the room is the state of your agents.

f1.title: The walk
f1.body: Real work earns a crossing: when an agent finishes a long task, it stands up, walks across the plan and waits at your desk until you've had a look. Discovering a finished agent twenty minutes late is over.

f2.title: Five states, zero reading
f2.body: Seated and working. Standing when it needs your input. Walking when it's done. At your desk for review. An empty seat when idle — plus a red cross when a turn fails. One glance covers them all.

f3.title: Calm by design
f3.body: When everyone is working, almost nothing moves — a monitor breathing, that's it. Native SwiftUI, no game-engine loop: the room costs about zero CPU while it sits with you all day.

f4.title: Desks are projects
f4.body: Each desk is one of your repositories, created the moment an agent first shows up there. Two agents can share a desk, and an empty desk is information too.

how.title: Three small pieces, all local

s1.title: A hook
s1.body: With your consent, Roster adds one line to ~/.claude/settings.json — after backing it up. From then on, every session event is appended to a local spool file.

s2.title: A spool file
s2.body: Events pile up even while Roster is closed. On launch the room replays them and catches up — no server, no socket, no polling.

s3.title: A room
s3.body: Events map one-to-one to the choreography: needs-input stands the agent up, a finished long turn triggers the walk, a failure pulls it back to its station.

how.privacy: Everything stays on your Mac. Roster never reads your code — only session events. No network, no account, no telemetry.

open.title: MIT, from day one
open.body: Roster is free and open source. The state machine is unit-tested, the fragile parts are isolated behind a thin layer, and the repo keeps a written log of every design decision. Good first issues are waiting for you.

q1.q: Does it work with agents other than Claude Code?
q1.a: Not yet. V0 is deliberately Claude Code + VS Code + one Mac — depth over breadth. The issue tracker is open if you want to change that.

q2.a: No. It only sees session events: state changes, the working directory, and the last assistant message for the summary. Nothing ever leaves your machine.

q3.q: Why isn't it on the Mac App Store?
q3.a: Roster needs to read ~/.claude and install its hook, which the App Store sandbox forbids. It ships as a signed, notarized DMG on GitHub Releases instead.

q4.q: What if Claude Code changes its file formats?
q4.a: The hooks Roster relies on are a documented interface, so the core is safe. The undocumented parts — the transcript bootstrap — are isolated and fail silently; worst case, the room misses a warm start.

cta.title: Put your agents in a room.
cta.body: One DMG, one hook, and your sessions become colleagues.

footer.tagline: Your coding agents, in a room. They come to your desk when they're done.
